questions.question: What will be the sum of number of Wednesdays, Thursdays and Fridays in February 2008?
questions.solution:
The given year is **2008**.

To check if it is a leap year: 2008 ÷ 4 = 502 (No remainder).

Since it is divisible by 4, **2008** is a **leap year**, and **February 2008** has **29 days**.

Now, we find the day of the week on **February 1, 2008**:

Using **January 1, 2008** as a reference (which was a **Tuesday**):

Days in **January** = 31 days.

Odd days in January = 31 ÷ 7 = 4 weeks and **3 odd days**.

Day on February 1 = Tuesday + 3 days = **Friday**.

Since **February 1st** is a **Friday** and the month has **29 days**, the day **Friday** will occur **5 times** (on the 1st, 8th, 15th, 22nd, and 29th).

All other days occur exactly **4 times** in the month.

Number of **Wednesdays** = 4

Number of **Thursdays** = 4

Number of **Fridays** = 5

Sum of the number of Wednesdays, Thursdays, and Fridays = 4 + 4 + 5 = **13**

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 4**”.

questions.question:
A clock shows the correct time at 12 PM. The clock gains 5 seconds every 10 minutes.

What time (in PM) will it show at 6 PM the same day?
questions.solution:
The time interval from **12 PM** to **6 PM** is:

6 PM − 12 PM = **6 hours**

Converting the total duration into minutes:

6 hours = 6 × 60 = **360 minutes**

The clock gains **5 seconds** every **10 minutes**. We first find how many **10-minute intervals** are there in 360 minutes:

Number of intervals = 360 ÷ 10 = **36 intervals**

Now, calculate the **total gain** in seconds:

Total gain = 36 × 5 = **180 seconds**

Convert the total gain from seconds into minutes:

Gain in minutes = 180 ÷ 60 = **3 minutes**

The clock was correct at 12 PM, so at 6 PM (actual time), the clock will show the actual time plus the gain:

Time shown = 6:00:00 + 0:03:00 = **6:03:00**

Hence, the clock will show **6:03:00** at 6 PM.

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 1**”.

questions.question:
5 years ago from present the ratio of L and M's age was 1 : 3. After 3 years from present their age will be in the ratio 2 : 5.

What is the respective ratio of present ages of L and M?
questions.solution:
Let the **present age** of **L** be **L** and the **present age** of **M** be **M**.

**5 years ago from the present**

 
 

 Age of **L**
 L − 5
 
 

 Age of **M**
 M − 5
 
 

**
The ratio of their ages was 1 : 3.

(L − 5) / (M − 5) = 1 / 3

3 × (L − 5) = 1 × (M − 5)

3L − 15 = M − 5

**M = 3L − 10** --- (Equation 1)

**After 3 years from the present**

 
 

 Age of **L**
 L + 3
 
 

 Age of **M**
 M + 3
 
 

The ratio of their ages will be 2 : 5.

(L + 3) / (M + 3) = 2 / 5

5 × (L + 3) = 2 × (M + 3)

5L + 15 = 2M + 6

**5L − 2M = −9** --- (Equation 2)

**Solving the Equations:**

Substitute the value of M from Equation 1 into Equation 2:

5L − 2 × (3L − 10) = −9

5L − 6L + 20 = −9

−L + 20 = −9

−L = −29

L = 29

Now, find the value of M using Equation 1:

M = 3 × 29 − 10

M = 87 − 10

M = 77

The **present age** of **L** is 29 and the **present age** of **M** is 77.

The **respective ratio** of their **present ages** (L : M) = **29 : 77**.

Hence, the correct answer is “Option 1**”.

questions.question: Tippani dance is a traditional folk dance of which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tippani** is a traditional folk dance originating from the **Saurashtra** region of **Gujarat**, specifically from coastal areas like **Chorwad** and **Veraval**.
 
• The dance is exclusively performed by women, particularly those belonging to the **Koli** and **Hali** communities, who traditionally worked as **laborers**.
 
• The name of the dance is derived from the tool used, the **Tippani**, which is a long wooden stick (about **175 cm**) with a wooden or iron block called a **Garbo** at the base.
 
• Historically, the dance evolved from the task of **beating lime** to level the floors and roofs during the construction of houses, where women used the sticks to create a rhythmic beat to alleviate their physical exhaustion.
 
• The performance features dancers striking the **Tippani** against the ground in synchronized movements, creating a powerful percussive rhythm that dictates the pace of the dance.
 
• Musical accompaniment includes folk instruments such as the **Zanj**, **Manjira**, **Tabla**, **Dhol**, and sometimes the **Shehnai**, with dancers singing traditional folk songs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maharashtra**:

 
 
• Famous for **Lavani**, a traditional song and dance genre performed to the beats of the **Dholki**.
 
• Other notable forms include **Koli** (the dance of the fishing community) and **Povada** (ballads describing historical events).
 
 
 
• **Rajasthan**:
 
 
• Renowned for the **Ghoomar** dance, traditionally performed by the **Bhil** tribe for the goddess **Saraswati**.
 
• Other dances include **Kalbelia** (recognized by **UNESCO**) and the balancing-act dance **Bhavai**.
 
 
 
• **Odisha**:
 
 
• Home to the classical dance **Odissi**, which is one of the oldest surviving dance forms in India.
 
• Prominent folk dances include **Chhau** (a martial arts dance), **Ghumura**, and **Sambalpuri**.
 
 
 
• **Gujarat**:
 
 
• Apart from **Tippani**, the state is famous for **Garba** and **Dandiya Raas**, which are globally popular during the **Navratri** festival.
 
• Other folk forms include the **Padhar** dance and the **Bhavai** folk drama.

__
 
• **Argon (Ar)** is a chemical element with atomic number **18** and is categorized as a **noble gas** within **Group 18** of the periodic table.
 
• In the Earth's atmosphere, **Argon** is the **third-most abundant gas**, comprising approximately **0.934%** (commonly rounded to **0.93%**) of dry air by volume.
 
• This gas is **monatomic** and chemically **inert**, which means it does not form stable chemical compounds at standard temperatures and pressures due to its complete **octet** of valence electrons.
 
• The majority of atmospheric Argon is **Argon-40**, which originates from the **radioactive decay** of **Potassium-40** found in the Earth's crust.
 
• It is significantly more abundant than other noble gases like **Neon** (0.0018%), **Helium** (0.0005%), and **Krypton** (0.0001%), making it the primary inert component after Nitrogen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Major Atmospheric Constituents**:

 
 
• **Nitrogen (78%)**: This is the most prevalent gas in the atmosphere, playing a crucial role in **biological molecules** like proteins and DNA via the **Nitrogen Cycle**.
 
• **Oxygen (21%)**: The second most abundant gas (approximately **20.95%**), essential for **aerobic respiration** and the process of **combustion**.
 
• **Carbon Dioxide (0.03%)**: Historically cited at **0.03%**, though modern levels exceed **0.04%**, it is a critical **greenhouse gas** and is indispensable for **photosynthesis** in plants.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Uses of Argon**:
 
 
• Used extensively in **incandescent lighting** and **fluorescent tubes** to prevent the oxidation of filaments.
 
• Commonly utilized as a **shielding gas** in **Gas Tungsten Arc Welding (GTAW)** to protect the weld area from atmospheric contaminants.
 
• Applied in **cryosurgery** and as a thermal insulator in **energy-efficient windows**.

questions.question: The longest glacier in India is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Siachen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Siachen Glacier** is located in the **Karakoram Range** in the **Himalayas**, near the **Line of Control (LoC)** between India and Pakistan.

questions.question: A light year is a measure of ___.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**distance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **light year** is a unit of **distance** rather than time, representing the total path covered by **light** in a **vacuum** over the duration of one **Julian year** (365.25 days).
 
• Light travels at an incredible velocity of approximately **299,792,458 meters per second** (roughly **3 × 10⁸ m/s**); when calculated over a full year, this distance equals approximately **9.46 trillion kilometers** (**9.46 × 10¹² km**).
 
• In the field of **astronomy**, standard terrestrial units like kilometers or miles are insufficient for measuring the immense voids of **interstellar space**, making the light year a fundamental metric for describing gaps between **stars** and **galaxies**.
 
• For instance, the nearest star to Earth (besides the Sun), **Proxima Centauri**, is about **4.24 light years** away, meaning its light takes over four years to reach our planet.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Time:** Measured in **seconds**, **minutes**, and **hours**, it defines the duration of events. While 'year' is a unit of time, 'light year' is strictly a spatial measurement.
 
• **Speed:** Refers to the rate of change of position, such as the **speed of light (c)**, which is a universal physical constant.
 
• **Mass:** A fundamental property of matter indicating its resistance to acceleration, typically measured in **kilograms (kg)** or **solar masses** in cosmic contexts.
 
• **Other Astronomical Units:**
 
 
• **Astronomical Unit (AU):** The average distance from the **Earth** to the **Sun**, approximately **150 million kilometers**.
 
• **Parsec (pc):** A unit used for even larger distances, equivalent to approximately **3.26 light years** or **3.08 × 10¹³ km**.

questions.question: During international competition of Judo, each match lasts for ___ minutes
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In accordance with the official regulations established by the **International Judo Federation (IJF)**, the standard duration for a competitive Judo match in the **Senior** category (for both men and women) is **4 minutes**.
 
• The **4-minute** rule represents **net combat time**, which means the clock is strictly paused whenever the referee calls **Mate** (to temporarily stop the contest) or **Sono-mama** (to freeze positions), and resumes only when the command **Hajime** is given.
 
• This unified timing of **4 minutes** was implemented to ensure **gender equality** across the sport, moving away from previous years where men’s matches lasted 5 minutes while women’s matches were 4 minutes.
 
• In **International Competition**, the same **4-minute** duration applies to the **Junior** age group (under 21), ensuring that athletes transitioning to the senior level are accustomed to the standard match length.
 
• If the **4-minute** regulation time expires and the athletes have equal scores or no scores at all, the match proceeds into an unlimited **Golden Score** period to determine a winner.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Golden Score Overtime**:

 
 
• There is no fixed time limit for the **Golden Score** phase; the first athlete to achieve any score (**Waza-ari** or **Ippon**) or the first to be disqualified by **Hansoku-make** (penalties) wins.
 
• All scores and **Shido** (minor penalties) recorded during the initial **4 minutes** are carried over into this sudden-death period.
 
 
 
• **Primary Scoring Actions**:
 
 
• **Ippon**: The highest score in Judo, awarded for a throw that lands the opponent largely on their back with **strength, speed, and control**, or for a submission (choke or armbar) and pinning for 20 seconds.
 
• **Waza-ari**: Awarded for a throw that lacks one of the elements of an Ippon or for a pin lasting between 10 and 19 seconds. Two **Waza-ari** scores equal an **Ippon**.
 
 
 
• **Age Category Variations**:
 
 
• While senior and junior international matches are **4 minutes**, certain **Cadet** (Under 18) and youth level competitions may occasionally utilize a **3-minute** or **2-minute** format depending on the specific tournament guidelines.

questions.question: What does the electromagnet do once it is activated in an electric bell?

options.text: Pulls the iron strip towards itself

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pulls the iron strip towards itself**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The functioning of an **electric bell** is based on the **magnetic effect of electric current**, where a coil of wire acts as a magnet when electricity passes through it.
 
• The main component is an **electromagnet**, which consists of **insulated copper wire** wound around a **soft iron core**.
 
• When the circuit is completed by pressing the switch, the current flows through the coil, creating a **magnetic field** that transforms the iron core into a temporary magnet.
 
• This **electromagnet** immediately exerts a force of attraction on the **iron strip** (also known as the **armature**) located nearby.
 
• As the **iron strip** is pulled toward the electromagnet, the **hammer** attached to it moves and strikes the **gong**, producing the ringing sound.
 
• This movement also causes the strip to move away from the **contact screw**, which results in the **breaking of the electrical circuit**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Core Components of an Electric Bell:**

 
 
• **Electromagnet**: A temporary magnet that only functions when current is present; the principle was first observed by **Hans Christian Oersted** in **1820**.
 
• **Soft Iron Armature**: Chosen because soft iron has high **magnetic permeability** and low **retentivity**, allowing it to be magnetized and demagnetized rapidly.
 
• **Contact Screw**: Serves as an adjustable component that maintains the **make-and-break** cycle of the circuit.
 
• **Hammer and Gong**: The mechanical parts responsible for converting the kinetic energy of the moving armature into **acoustic energy**.
 
• **Spring Strip**: Provides the restoring force to bring the **iron strip** back to the contact screw once the magnetism is lost, enabling a continuous ringing cycle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Pakhawaj**:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nuclear fusion** is the process where two light atomic nuclei combine to form a single heavier nucleus, a transformation that releases a vast amount of energy due to the conversion of mass into energy according to **Einstein mass-energy equivalence**.
 
• The primary nuclei used in this process are **Hydrogen and its isotopes**, specifically **Deuterium (²H)** and **Tritium (³H)**, because their low atomic number (Z=1) results in the lowest possible **Coulombic repulsion** between nuclei.
 
• The **Deuterium-Tritium (D-T) reaction** is the most widely pursued for energy production because it has a high reaction cross-section at relatively lower temperatures, roughly **150 million degrees Celsius**.
 
• A single D-T fusion event produces a **Helium-4** nucleus and a high-energy **neutron**, yielding approximately **17.6 MeV** of energy per reaction.
 
• While **Deuterium** is abundantly found in Earth oceans, **Tritium** is rare and is typically bred from **Lithium** within the fusion reactor blanket during operation.

questions.question: 77 - 33 + 28 of 2 + 46 ÷ 2 - 17 + (29) = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **BODMAS rule** sequentially: **Of** → **Division** → **Addition/Subtraction**.

Calculate priority operations: 28 of 2 = 56 and 46 ÷ 2 = 23.

Combine all positive terms: 77 + 56 + 23 + 29 = 185.

Combine all negative terms: −33 − 17 = −50.

Net result: 185 − 50 = 135.

**∴ The correct answer is 135.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 77 − 33 + 28 of 2 + 46 ÷ 2 − 17 + 29

**Formula Used:** **BODMAS rule** (Brackets, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

⇒ 77 − 33 + (28 × 2) + 46 ÷ 2 − 17 + 29

⇒ 77 − 33 + 56 + (46 ÷ 2) − 17 + 29

⇒ 77 − 33 + 56 + 23 − 17 + 29

⇒ 44 + 56 + 23 − 17 + 29

⇒ 100 + 23 − 17 + 29

⇒ 123 − 17 + 29

⇒ 106 + 29 = 135

**∴ The correct answer is 135.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS / VBODMAS Rule

This rule defines the order of priority: **V** (Vinculum/Bar), **B** (Brackets), **O** (Of), **D** (Division), **M** (Multiplication), **A** (Addition), and **S** (Subtraction).

The 'Of' Operator

The word **'of'** serves as a multiplication operator but must be calculated **before** any division or standard multiplication in the expression.

Group Calculation Trick

To avoid sign errors in long expressions, sum all **positive numbers** and **negative numbers** separately before performing the final subtraction.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Perform the **decimal divisions** directly by balancing the number of decimal places.

First term: 0.08 ÷ 0.4 = 0.8 ÷ 4 = 0.2

Second term: 0.024 ÷ 0.6 = 0.24 ÷ 6 = 0.04

Difference = 0.2 − 0.04 = 0.16

**∴ The correct answer is 0.16.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** (0.08 / 0.4) − (0.024 / 0.6)

According to the **BODMAS rule**, division operations must be completed before subtraction.

⇒ Term 1 = 0.08 ÷ 0.4 = (8 / 100) ÷ (4 / 10)

⇒ Term 1 = (8 / 100) × (10 / 4) = 80 / 400 = 1 / 5 = 0.2

⇒ Term 2 = 0.024 ÷ 0.6 = (24 / 1000) ÷ (6 / 10)

⇒ Term 2 = (24 / 1000) × (10 / 6) = 240 / 6000 = 4 / 100 = 0.04

⇒ Final Value = 0.2 − 0.04 = 0.16

**∴ The correct answer is 0.16.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

In mathematical calculations, always follow the sequence: **Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction**.

Decimal Conversion

To simplify division with decimals, multiply both numerator and denominator by 10ⁿ to convert them into **whole numbers**.

Subtraction of Decimals

While subtracting decimals like 0.2 and 0.04, ensure the **decimal points** are aligned vertically by adding a placeholder zero (e.g., 0.20 − 0.04).

(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²

**Calculations:**

⇒ (7.75 + 2.75)² − 4 × 7.75 × 2.75

⇒ (10.5)² − (4 × 21.3125)

⇒ 110.25 − 85.25

⇒ 25

Algebraic Identity - Square of Sum

The expression (a + b)² expands to a² + 2ab + b².

Algebraic Identity - Square of Difference

Relationship between Sum and Difference Squares

The identities are related as (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab and (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²).

questions.question: If √210.25 = 14.5, then what is the value of √0.00021025?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In **square root** calculations, if the **decimal point** shifts by 2n places inside the root, it shifts by n places in the result.

Movement inside √ : 210.25 → 0.00021025 (6 places to the left).

Movement in result : 14.5 → (6 ÷ 2 = 3 places to the left).

Final Value : 14.5 → 0.0145.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.0145.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** √210.25 = 14.5

We need to find the value of **√0.00021025**.

⇒ 0.00021025 = 210.25 ÷ 1,000,000

⇒ 0.00021025 = 210.25 ÷ 10⁶

Taking **square root** on both sides:

⇒ √0.00021025 = √(210.25 ÷ 10⁶)

⇒ √0.00021025 = √210.25 ÷ √10⁶

⇒ √0.00021025 = 14.5 ÷ 10³

⇒ √0.00021025 = 14.5 ÷ 1000

⇒ √0.00021025 = 0.0145

**∴ The correct answer is 0.0145.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square Root of Powers of 10

The square root of 10²ⁿ is always 10ⁿ. For example, √100 = 10 and √10,000 = 100.

Decimal Rule in Square Roots

For every two decimal places inside a **square root**, there is one decimal place in the square root's value (e.g., √0.01 = 0.1).

Squares of Numbers Ending in 5

To square a number like 14.5, multiply 14 by 15 (210) and append 0.25 to get 210.25.

questions.question: What is the sum of all prime numbers between 20 and 40?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

List all **Prime Numbers** between 20 and 40: 23, 29, 31, 37.

Group them for faster calculation: (23 + 37) + (29 + 31).

Sum = 60 + 60 = 120.

**∴ The correct answer is 120.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Range for prime numbers is 20 to 40.

A **Prime Number** is a natural number greater than 1 that has no positive divisors other than 1 and itself.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/22f6093a308853b9d52364e8a30ae5d82a2b01c8a0baed1774f2fd0a9f2d875d.png] 

**Step-by-step Calculation:**

⇒ Odd numbers between 20 and 40: 21, 23, 25, 27, 29, 31, 33, 35, 37, 39.

⇒ Eliminate non-primes: 21 (3×7), 25 (5×5), 27 (3×9), 33 (3×11), 35 (5×7), 39 (3×13).

⇒ Remaining primes: 23, 29, 31, 37.

⇒ Total Sum = 23 + 29 + 31 + 37

⇒ Total Sum = 52 + 68

⇒ Total Sum = 120

**∴ The correct answer is 120.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Prime Numbers Definition

A **Prime Number** has only two factors: 1 and the number itself. The smallest prime number is 2, and it is the only even prime.

Composite Numbers

Numbers with more than two factors are called **Composite Numbers**. 1 is neither prime nor composite.

Primes up to 100

There are exactly 25 prime numbers between 1 and 100. The sum of prime numbers from 1 to 50 is 328.

questions.question: (15)³ + (5)³ + 3 × 15 × 5 × 20 = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the algebraic identity: **a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b) = (a + b)³**.

In the given expression, let **a = 15** and **b = 5**, which means **a + b = 20**.

The expression becomes: (15 + 5)³ ⇒ 20³.

Result = 20 × 20 × 20 = 8000.

**∴ The correct answer is 8000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (15)³ + (5)³ + 3 × 15 × 5 × 20

**Formula Used:** (a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3a²b + 3ab² = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b)

⇒ Let **a = 15** and **b = 5**.

⇒ The sum of **a** and **b** is 15 + 5 = 20.

⇒ Substituting these into the formula: 15³ + 5³ + 3 × 15 × 5 × (15 + 5).

⇒ This is exactly the same as (15 + 5)³.

⇒ (20)³ = 20 × 20 × 20 = 8000.

**∴ The correct answer is 8000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cube of Difference Identity

The identity for the cube of a difference is (a − b)³ = a³ − b³ − 3ab(a − b).

Sum of Cubes Factorization

The expression a³ + b³ can be factored as (a + b)(a² − ab + b²).

Difference of Cubes Factorization

The expression a³ − b³ can be factored as (a − b)(a² + ab + b²).

questions.question: The perimeter of a rectangle is 24 cm. The length of the rectangle is 5 cm. What is the sum (in cm) of length and breadth of the rectangle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **rectangle**, the **perimeter** is twice the sum of its **length** and **breadth**.

Sum of (Length + Breadth) = Perimeter ÷ 2

Given Perimeter = 24 cm

∴ Sum = 24 ÷ 2 = 12 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Perimeter of **rectangle** = 24 cm

Length (L) = 5 cm

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter = 2 × (Length + Breadth)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/32c943ca5679f428c5462faef638a4706f01e335eb32904fab2a491d2ea2ea38.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 24 = 2 × (5 + Breadth)

⇒ 24 ÷ 2 = 5 + Breadth

⇒ 12 = 5 + Breadth

⇒ Breadth = 12 − 5 = 7 cm

⇒ Sum of length and breadth = 5 + 7 = 12 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Rectangle

The total space occupied by the rectangle is calculated as Length × Breadth.

Diagonal of Rectangle

The distance between opposite corners is given by √(Length² + Breadth²).

Perimeter of Square

For a square where all sides (a) are equal, the perimeter is 4 × a.

Relationship of Perimeter and Sides

The semi-perimeter of a rectangle is exactly equal to the sum of its adjacent sides (L + B).

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

questions.question: If x = sqrt{1671 + sqrt{93 + sqrt{49}}} , then what is the value of x?

Solve the **nested radical** expression mentally from the **innermost root** outwards.

√49 = 7

√(93 + 7) = √100 = 10

√(1671 + 10) = √1681 = 41

**∴ The correct answer is 41.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x = √(1671 + √(93 + √49))

**Formula Used:**

For any non-negative number a, √a² = a

**Calculations:**

⇒ x = √(1671 + √(93 + 7))

⇒ x = √(1671 + √100)

⇒ x = √(1671 + 10)

⇒ x = √1681

⇒ x = √(41²)

⇒ x = 41

**∴ The correct answer is 41.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perfect Square Identification

To find √1681, observe that 40² = 1600. Since 1681 ends in 1, the **square root** must end in either 1 or 9. Thus, 41 is the most likely candidate.

BODMAS in Radicals

In **nested radicals**, the **order of operations** dictates that the innermost grouping (the smallest radical) must be simplified before moving to the outer layers.

Unit Digit Rule

Numbers ending in 1, 4, 5, 6, or 9 can be **perfect squares**. A number ending in 1 will have a square root ending in 1 or 9.

questions.question: 84P6 is divisible by 6. Which of the following cannot be the value of P?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A number is **divisible by 6** if it is divisible by both **2** and **3**.

84P6 ends in 6 (even), so it is divisible by 2.

Sum of digits = 8 + 4 + P + 6 = 18 + P must be a multiple of 3.

Checking options: 18 + 0 = 18, 18 + 3 = 21, 18 + 9 = 27 are all divisible by 3.

However, 18 + 7 = 25 is not divisible by 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The number **84P6** is divisible by 6.

**Formula:** For a number to be divisible by 6, it must satisfy the divisibility rules of both 2 and 3.

⇒ **Divisibility by 2:** The last digit of 84P6 is 6, which is an even number. Thus, the number is divisible by 2 for any digit value of P.

⇒ **Divisibility by 3:** The sum of the digits must be divisible by 3.

⇒ Sum = 8 + 4 + P + 6 = 18 + P.

⇒ For (18 + P) to be divisible by 3, P must be 0, 3, 6, or 9 (since 18 is already divisible by 3).

⇒ **Testing Option 1:** If P = 0, Sum = 18 + 0 = 18 (Divisible by 3).

⇒ **Testing Option 2:** If P = 3, Sum = 18 + 3 = 21 (Divisible by 3).

⇒ **Testing Option 3:** If P = 9, Sum = 18 + 9 = 27 (Divisible by 3).

⇒ **Testing Option 4:** If P = 7, Sum = 18 + 7 = 25 (NOT divisible by 3).

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 3

A number is divisible by 3 if the **sum of all its digits** is divisible by 3.

Divisibility Rule of 4

A number is divisible by 4 if the **last two digits** of the number are divisible by 4 or are both zero.

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the **sum of its digits** is a multiple of 9.

questions.question: The average of 10 numbers is X and one of these numbers is 30. If 30 is replaced with 10, then what will be the new average?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the **net change** in the total sum: New value − Old value = 10 − 30 = −20.

Calculate the **change in average**: Net change ÷ Total numbers = −20 ÷ 10 = −2.

New average = Old average + Change in average = X + (−2) = X − 2.

**∴ The correct answer is X − 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total numbers = 10

Initial average = X

Old number = 30

New number = 10

**Formula used:**

Sum = Average × Count

New Average = (Total Sum − Old Number + New Number) ÷ Count

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cdc38071882882542088e7cc45fb49c3d65ab0608451175fe88a732f956f21c2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total initial sum = 10 × X = 10X

⇒ New sum = 10X − 30 + 10

⇒ New sum = 10X − 20

⇒ New average = (10X − 20) ÷ 10

⇒ New average = 10X/10 − 20/10

⇒ New average = X − 2

**∴ The correct answer is X − 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

General Average Formula

The **average** (Arithmetic Mean) is defined as Sum of observations ÷ Total number of observations.

Effect of Replacement

When one value is replaced, the **new average** = Old average + (Difference ÷ n), where Difference = New value − Old value and n = total items.

Uniform Change Property

If every number in a set is increased or decreased by a constant value **k**, the **average** also increases or decreases by exactly **k**.

questions.question: A is 20 percent less than B. B is how much percentage more than A?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert **percentage** to **fraction**: 20% = 1/5.

If A is 1/5 **less** than B, then the numerator remains 1 and the denominator becomes (5 − 1) = 4.

B is 1/4 **more** than A.

1/4 × 100 = 25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** A is 20% less than B.

**Formula:** Percentage more = [(Difference) ÷ (Lesser Value)] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f8dca706d93c9f3c4a0c7f211aef1c021ccb5c5710641bb6cc68bdea442a70a1.png] 

⇒ Let the value of **B** = 100.

⇒ Value of **A** = 100 − 20% of 100 = 80.

⇒ Difference between **B** and **A** = 100 − 80 = 20.

⇒ Percentage by which **B** is more than **A** = (Difference ÷ A) × 100.

⇒ Percentage more = (20 ÷ 80) × 100.

⇒ Percentage more = (1 ÷ 4) × 100 = 25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Base Change Formula

If A is x% less than B, then B is [x ÷ (100 − x)] × 100% more than A.

Fractional Equivalence

Common percentages to remember: 20% = 1/5, 25% = 1/4, 33.33% = 1/3, 50% = 1/2.

Successive Percentage Change

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
The gardener was pruning the hedges when the fog rolled in.

options.text: The hedges were been pruning by the gardener when the fog rolled in.

The hedges were pruned by the gardener when the fog rolled in.
The hedges were being pruned by the gardener when the fog rolled in.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The hedges were being pruned by the gardener when the fog rolled in.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The original sentence is in the **Past Continuous Tense**, characterized by the structure: **Subject + was/were + verb(-ing) + object**. In this case, **The gardener** is the subject, **was pruning** is the verb, and **the hedges** is the object.

• To transform a sentence from **Active Voice** to **Passive Voice** in the **Past Continuous Tense**, the following formula is applied: **New Subject + was/were + being + Past Participle (V3) + by + New Object**.

• Since the object **the hedges** is **plural**, it becomes the new subject and takes the plural auxiliary verb **were**.

• The word **being** must be added to maintain the **continuous aspect** of the original sentence, followed by the third form (past participle) of the verb prune, which is **pruned**.

• The phrase **when the fog rolled in** is a subordinate **adverbial clause of time** and remains unchanged at the end of the sentence to provide the necessary context.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Understanding Voice and Tense**:

• **Passive Voice**: This construction is used when the focus is shifted from the person performing the action (the gardener) to the recipient of the action (the hedges).

• **Common Errors**: Using **were pruned** without **being** changes the tense to **Simple Past Passive**, which incorrectly implies a completed action rather than an ongoing one.

• **Invalid Auxiliary Combinations**: Phrases like **were been** are grammatically incorrect in English because **been** is reserved for **Perfect Tenses** (e.g., have been, had been), not continuous passive structures.

• **Agreement**: Subject-verb agreement is crucial; a plural subject like **hedges** always requires **were** rather than **was**.

</ul

A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. If you feel Options A, B, or C do not improve the sentence, then choose Option D: "No improvement required."

options.text: The rigorous training program, having been completed by the employees
Having completed the employees rigorous training program,
Having completed the rigorous training program, the employees

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Having completed the rigorous training program, the employees**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The original sentence contains a grammatical error in the formation of the **perfect participle**. The structure **having completing** is incorrect because the auxiliary verb **having** must be followed by the **past participle** (V3) form of the verb, which is **completed**.

• The **perfect participle** (having + past participle) is specifically used to denote an action that was finished before another action began. Here, the completion of the **rigorous training program** occurred prior to the employees feeling **well prepared**.

• The correct choice places the **participle phrase** at the beginning of the sentence. This creates a clear **introductory modifier** that logically refers to the subject **the employees**, who appear immediately after the comma.

• By restructuring the sentence this way, the **syntactic flow** is improved, removing the awkward parenthetical interruption found in the original sentence and ensuring the **chronological sequence** of events is clearly communicated.

• This correction adheres to the rules of **subject-modifier agreement**, where the person or thing performing the action in the participle phrase must be the grammatical subject of the main clause.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Participle Phrases**:

• **Perfect Participle**: Formed by **having + past participle**. It indicates a completed action (e.g., **Having finished** the work, he left).

• **Present Participle**: Formed by **V-ing**. It usually indicates an action happening simultaneously with the main verb (e.g., **Walking** down the street, I saw him).

• **Misplaced and Dangling Modifiers**:

• A **misplaced modifier** occurs when the descriptive phrase is too far from the noun it modifies. In Option 1, the **rigorous training program** is the subject, which would imply the program itself **felt well prepared**, resulting in a logical error.

• A **dangling modifier** happens when the intended subject of the modifier is missing from the sentence entirely.

• **Passive Voice Construction**:

• Option 1 uses a **passive perfect participle** (having been completed), which unnecessarily complicates the sentence and shifts the focus away from the **employees** as the active participants.

</ul

• The word **drive** is the plural form of the verb in the **simple present tense**, which is appropriate for stating a general fact or ongoing trend.

• **driving**: This is the **continuous** or **progressive** form. It requires an auxiliary verb like 'are' (e.g., 'Startups **are driving**') to function as the main verb of the sentence.
 
• **driven**: This is the **past participle**. It requires an auxiliary verb like 'have' for the perfect tense (e.g., 'Startups **have driven**') or 'are' for the passive voice.
